title: Malcolm Todd’s ‘Earrings’ Leads Top Gabb Music Songs for Second Month
summary: The track reigns over a slew of songs by women, led by Stella Lefty’s “Boston.”
contentText:
Malcolm Todd ’s “Earrings” is No. 1 on the Top Gabb Music Songs chart for the second month in a row, crowning the September 2026 survey after first reigning over the August list.

Billboard has partnered with Gabb Wireless, a phone company for kids and teens, to present a monthly chart, which launched in October 2024, tracking on-demand streams via its Gabb Music platform. Gabb Music offers a vast catalog of songs, all of which are selected by the Gabb team to include only kid- and teen-appropriate content. Gabb Music streams are not currently factored into any other Billboard charts.

“Earrings” reached a new peak of No. 19 on the weekly Billboard Hot 100 in September and did not depart the top 20 for the entire month.

The track, which was originally released in 2024, has spent three months on Top Gabb Music Songs; it debuted at No. 9 on the July 2026 tally.

“Earrings” leads the chart over Stella Lefty ’s “Boston,” which rises five positions to a new peak of No. 2. Like “Earrings,” “Boston” also debuted on the July 2026 survey, bowing at No. 21.

“Boston” spent the entirety of September at its peak so far of No. 2 on the Hot 100, while her album Long Way Home started at No. 11 on the Billboard 200 dated Sept. 5.

In all, the top 10 of Top Gabb Music Songs features seven songs performed by women for September, the most in any month since the ranking’s October 2024 inception. Two of those are by the same act: Olivia Rodrigo , whose “The Cure” and “Deja Vu” appear at Nos. 8 and 9, respectively.

Two of those songs are also newcomers to the region. Alyssa Grace’s “Bloodstream” zooms 16 positions to No. 4, while KATSEYE is the month’s top debut with “Hootie Frutti” at No. 6. The former returned to its peak of No. 45 on the Hot 100 in September, and the latter bowed at No. 31 on the tally at the end of August.

And following her Aug. 25 death, Dolly Parton ’s “9 to 5” becomes the country singer’s first Top Gabb Music Songs appearance, debuting at No. 20.
